The Sub-Inspector of Police, J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 323, 324, 498A and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the marriage of the sister of the informant was solemnized with abated accused No.1 as per their custom.
Accused No.2 is the brother of the accused No.1 and abated accused No.3 is the mother of the accused No.1.
All these accused have taken dowry of Rs.50,000/- at the time of marriage.
The sister of the informant Sumangala was happy with accused No.1 for some days.
Later, these accused persons stated torturing Sumangala for further dowry.
They tortured physically and mentally.
On the information of this torture, the parents of Sumangala had been to the accused and requested them not to torture her daughter physically and mentally.
These accused sent Sumangala for delivery and never came back to take Sumangala to their house.
They had been to them and requested to take back this Sumangala to their house.
However, they refused and sent them back by using filthy language.
They started abusing the Sumangala that she gave birth to a female child.
Soon after the incident, the informant had not been to the Police Station as because they were thinking that these accused one or the other day will mend their behaviours.
On 05.08.2001, they had been to the house of the accused to appease them again.

But, however,
they started shouting them in a filthy language and demanded further dowry.
The accused No.1 in furtherance of his act assaulted the Sumangala with rod on her head and caused grievous injuries.
The other accused instigated accused No.1 to assault Sumangala.
Soon after the incident, the informant had been to the police station and lodged the information against the accused persons.
3. After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to accused No.1 to 3.
On 13.08.2001, accused No.1 and 2 were enlarged on bail.
On 15.09.2001 accused No.3 was enlarged on bail.
As per order sheet dated 08.03.2024, accused No.3 was reported as dead.
Hence, the case against her was abated.
As per order sheet dated 13.02.2024, accused No.1 was reported as dead.
Hence, the case against him was also abated.
Accused No.2 was enlarged on bail on 13.02.2024.
The copies of the Police Report and other Prosecution papers are furnished to accused No.2 under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that accused No.2 has committed the offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences punishable under Section 323,
324, 498A and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code has been framed and read over to accused No.2 in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused No.2, the Prosecution has examined PW1 and PW2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P5.

After completion of the Prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling accused No.2 personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined accused No.2 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned Counsel for accused No.2.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are:-
1.

Whether prosecution has proved the offences charged against accused No.2 persons for the offences punishable under Section 323, 324, 498A and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt?
2. What order or sentence?

7. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following;
 REASONS 8. POINT No.1 :- It is the case of the Prosecution that all these accused tortured the Sumangala who is the sister of the informant physically and mentally.
These accused were demanding further dowry even though they have taken huge dowry of Rs.50,000/- at the time of marriage.
During the course of trial, the accused No.1 and 3 were reported dead and the case against them was abated.

Accused No.2 is the brother of the late accused No.1.
9.
To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 who is the First Informant of this case and she has deposed that the marriage of her sister was solemnized with accused No.1.
Accused No.2 is the brother of accused No.1 and accused No.3 is the mother of accused No.1.
They have taken dowry of Rs.50,000/- at the time of marriage.
Her sister was happy with the accused No.1 for some days.
Later, they started demanding more dowry.
They had been to them and advised not to torture her sister physically and mentally.
Later, these accused sent her sister to her house for delivery and never turned back when her sister gave birth to a female child.
They started demanding Rs.50,000/- to take back her sister.
They had been to them and requested to take their sister Sumangala.
But, however they refused and demanded Rs.50,000/- further dowry.
Again, they had been to their house along with Sumangala.
But, however the accused No.1 assaulted this Sumangala with club.
Accused No.2 assaulted him with iron rod.
Accused No.3 caught hold of her sister and instigated other accused to assault them.
10. The Prosecution has examined CW9/PW2 who is an Investigation Officer, wherein he has deposed that on 05.08.2001 he has registered the information of CW1 and registered the FIR.
He had been to the place of incident and conducted panchanama in the presence of CW2 and CW3.
After completion of investigation, he has lodged the Final Report against these accused.

sentences.text: It is the case of the Prosecution that accused No.1 is the husband of the sister of the informant and accused No.2 is the brother of accused No.1.
Accused No.3 is the mother of accused No.1.
These accused have taken dowry of Rs.50,000/- at the time of marriage and again the put their demand of Rs.50,000/-.
They have tortured the sister of the informant Sumangala physically and mentally.
This accused No.1 assaulted the sister of the informant with an iron rod on her head and caused grievous injuries.
Accused No.2 assaulted this CW1 with club and caused injuries.

Accused No.3 instigated accused No.1 and 2.
12.
To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 who has deposed as per his information Ex.P1.

This matter is pending since 2001 and in spite of sufficient opportunities,
the Prosecution has not able to examine the rest of the witnesses.
The only evidence available before this Court is the evidence of CW1.
The accused No.1 and 3 were reported dead.
CW1 has deposed that this accused No.2 assaulted him with a club on her back and caused grievous injuries.

But,
however, the Prosecution has not examined CW8 who has examined and issued Wound Certificate.

Further, it is the case of the Prosecution that as per the PF submitted by the Investigation Officer,
the Investigation Officer has seized one club and one rod from the place of incident by conducting the seizure panchanama in the presence of panchas. But, however the Prosecution has not examined these CW2 and CW3 panchas who were alleged to be present at the time of incident.
The only evidence available before this Court is the evidence of CW1.

My Predecessor by giving sufficient opportunities to the Prosecution to examine the rest of the witnesses and also by issuing summons,
warrants and Proclamation and dropped the rest of the witnesses.

The matter is pending since more than 25 years and accordingly, this Court finds that as there is no evidence before this Court to prove the guilt of accused No.2, hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

13. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 324, 498A and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, accused No.2 is not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against him.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.2 is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 323, 324, 498A and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

His bail bond and surety bond executed will be in force till completion of appeal period and thereafter, it will be stand canceled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court, today this the 30 th day of September 2024)
(SAHEEL AHMED.S.KUNNIBHAVI) II Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
